messages:
maya: Customer reported streaming responses cut off mid-token, then client reconnects and immediately gets 401. Billing shows a spike of small short-lived sessions. Using ALB -> cloudflare -> origin. Seen across two customers. Anyone seen auth flaps on reconnect?

chris: Which endpoint? streaming /v1/responses or chat?

maya: /v1/responses streaming SSE. Repro steps attached below from customer. They use Cloudflare with origin keepalives enabled and ALB in front of our instances.

alice: note: billing spike makes me think client is retrying on every silent disconnect. Could be idle timeout + client auto-reconnect. 401 on reconnect could be token rotation mismatch.

ivan: can you paste the curl + headers they used? small things like Connection: keep-alive vs close matter with ALB+CF.

maya: customer logs: ```
> curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses/stream
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 10:02:12 GMT
transfer-encoding: chunked
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
...
data: {"id":"tok_abc","text":"Hello wor"\n\n# connection goes silent for ~35s (no bytes), client reconnects
> curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses/stream
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json

{"error":"token_expired"}
```

chris: idle ~35s is suspicious. ALB idle timeout default is 60s but Cloudflare may probe. But silence leading to mid-chunk cutoff suggests intermediate buffering. Do we see any proxy half-close in our logs?

sre-bot: Deploy log: instance-redux-21 connection from ALB 10.0.5.32 terminated (RST) at 2025-10-14T10:02:47Z.

ivan: can we get raw connection traces? customer said TLS terminated at Cloudflare then proxied to ALB. CF sometimes buffers until full chunk or certain flush thresholds. ALB->nginx could be squashing tiny writes.

alice: Also check token refresh flow on their client: if client refreshes token after initial connect and then reconnects using a new token, but our token revocation or session mapping may reject old session / accept new only. The 401 on reconnect is weird: expected 200 if token valid. Do we return 401 for mismatched session id?

maya: From support logs: two different clients from same customer saw identical pattern. We captured x-request-id: req_0a1b2c and req_0a1b3d. Request headers included `Connection: keep-alive`, `Accept: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`.

chris: Repro attempt: I ran a local loop that pauses writing small chunks every 20s behind an nghttp2 proxy; I saw the client library close after 30s of silence. So client reconnect + retry on silence seems plausible. Need to know where silence originates.

ivan: Next steps for triage: 1) Get packet-level pcap or tcpdump for the time window (ALB -> origin). 2) Ask Cloudflare config: are they using HTTP/2 to origin, or buffering (Argo/Cache tier)? 3) Check our ingress proxy (nginx/envoy) for `proxy_buffering` or `http2` flow control and flush thresholds.

alice: Also check auth logs: show token validation path for `req_0a1b3d`. If token was still valid on reconnect time we should have accepted. If we revoked due to session reuse, need to record that.

maya: I added the customer to a private repro workspace and asked for exact CF config + ALB target group idle timeout. They replied: CF -> origin set to HTTP/2, origin idle probe 30s, ALB idle timeout 35s.

chris: aha CF origin idle 30s + ALB 35s could interact badly. If CF closes upstream connection silently, ALB might RST and we see half-chunk. The 401 likely due to client trying to reuse a short-lived rotating token.

ivan: Can engineering confirm whether we flush after every SSE event, or we rely on buffer coalescing? If we batch small writes, proxies may decide to hold until threshold. Code snippet from runtime: ```
// send SSE event
socket.write(`data: ${payload}\n\n`); // no explicit flush
```

alice: if runtime doesn't call `socket.flush()` equivalent, some proxies or the OS can buffer. But SSE requires timely byte flushing. We should add explicit flush or write with proper chunk sizes. Also consider sending a heartbeat comment `: keepalive` every 15s to keep middleboxes from idling.

maya: Customer agreed to try: 1) enable `send keepalive comments every 15s` client-facing toggle, 2) set CF origin keepalive > 60s and ALB timeout >= 60s temporarily, 3) confirm client token refresh behavior to avoid 401 during reconnect.

chris: Action items: @ivan take packet dump request and examine RST/FIN sequence. @alice check auth logs for req ids and whether token was expired or rejected for another reason. @maya coordinate with customer on CF/ALB settings and keepalive experiment. I'll loop in eng-runtime if we find evidence of missing flush/heartbeat.

ivan: I'll pull tcpdump and post 10s around events. If upstream is sending FIN without data then the cut-off is upstream. If we see keepalive probes dropped, we can indicate proxy buffering.

sre-bot: Created incident INC-2025-1987 for streaming-edge-proxy-idle. Assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

maya: Thanks all — customer on call at 15:00 PT, will update after we have packet traces. :thumbsup:
